_note: Habitation zone. People live in family homes, in five suite tiers from simple to presidential. Each step up houses fewer people per slot, draws more power, water and timber, and buys more morale — the housing choice is a standard-of-living policy expressed in build slots. The common hall raises morale AND assembly risk: a direct hook from the sim layer into the political layer.

buildings.name: Simple suite
buildings._note: The bottom rung: families packed into one-room homes. Cheapest housing per slot in the Shaft, and everyone can tell.

buildings.name: Superior suite
buildings._note: The first tier that consumes timber for fittings. From here up, housing people well is a resource decision the player has to defend.

buildings.name: Presidential suite
buildings._note: Four slots on the most desirable levels for a dozen people. The few who live here are content; everyone else can see the lights on upstairs. Costs trust and feeds assembly risk for as long as it stands.

buildings.name: Canteen
buildings._note: The canteen is where people eat, which is what makes it the destination for every food haul. Distance from the hydroponics bay is therefore paid in porter-hours every single day, forever — placement is permanent policy. The rations themselves are drawn per head (population.foodPerCapitaPerTick); the canteen's own 1 food a tick is kitchen loss, and with an empty larder it is starved and its morale goes with it.

buildings.name: Clinic
buildings._note: Sits at 'medical' on the priority ladder, above industry and below water. Whether the clinic outranks the workshop is a decision the player makes early and feels much later. Its consumable supply chain is still an open design item.

buildings.name: School
buildings._note: Consumes paper, and so competes with the Accord for the same timber. Educating children and writing law draw on one stock.

buildings.name: Common hall
buildings._note: The clearest sim-to-politics hook in the game. People are happier because they can gather, and they can gather because they are together. Sealing it during unrest costs exactly the morale that was holding things steady.

buildings.name: Auditorium
buildings._note: Six slots and unmovable: the hall was built before the player and takes most of the top level. Six and not seven because 384 px is the widest room the generator will draw in one pass (probe/v26). It is the only room that can hold the whole Shaft at once, which is what makes it worth its slots and what makes it dangerous — the assembly risk here is the highest of any building. Its back window shows a dead plain, and it is a screen; the room is where a departure through the Exit on this level is watched.
